description: Soy Angel, abogado y especialista en IA y software de Lima. Trabajo con modelos de lenguaje, sistemas RAG, automatización con agentes y desarrollo web en Python. Me interesan los datos de ciencias de la Tierra y cómo convertirlos en herramientas útiles para cualquier persona. Participo en solitario.
summary:
EarthTrend Detective, with its assistant Huiracocha AI, turns students into data detectives. Choose any place on Earth, or ask a question in English or Spanish, and it retrieves real NASA data (NASA POWER, GISTEMP and the NSIDC Sea Ice Index), shows how a variable has changed over up to 45 years, and answers the four questions of the challenge: what is changing, where, how much, and whether the change is statistically significant.

It gives honest verdicts: a verdict gets stronger only when independent tests agree after correcting for autocorrelation; when they disagree the tool shows it, and when the record is too short it estimates how many more years are needed. Its assistant, built with retrieval over 999 documents (RAG) and an optional LoRA-tuned planner, covers five Peruvian cities in depth, and a guard rejects any number that is not in the statistical result.

It matters because climate claims are everywhere and rarely checked. EarthTrend Detective lets students and teachers verify them in one click, in Spanish or English, with no account and no installation, and learn that real science means quantifying uncertainty.
details:
EarthTrend Detective, with its assistant Huiracocha AI, turns students into data detectives. Pick any place on Earth or ask a question in English or Spanish ("Is it raining less in Ica?"): the tool fetches the real NASA series for that place, shows how it changed over up to 45 years and answers the four questions of the challenge: WHAT is changing, WHERE, HOW MUCH, and whether the change is STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Plan: the question becomes a plan (variable, place, period). Deterministic rules always decide; in the live demo a language model proposes the plan first and the rules overrule it when they disagree.

2. Retrieve: live NASA POWER (MERRA-2 and CERES) monthly data for 35 variables, plus NASA GISTEMP and the NSIDC Sea Ice Index. Every series stores its exact request URL, retrieval time and sha256.

3. Analyse: Theil-Sen slope with a 95% interval, Mann-Kendall with the Hamed-Rao autocorrelation correction, an adjusted t-test and a detectability estimate. A verdict is rated "strong" only when all the tests agree and the record is long enough; when they disagree the tool says so. "Scan all variables" tests every variable for a place with Benjamini-Hochberg correction.

4. Answer and cite: a plain-language answer with a verdict and the years of data still needed, with sources from a retrieval corpus (RAG) of 999 documents from 172 publishers (NASA, NOAA, SENAMHI, ANA, IGP, INAIGEM and peer-reviewed papers; 340 of them are trends computed by our own engine and never shown as quotations). It is documented in depth for five Peruvian cities: Lima, Huancayo, Andahuaylas, Ica and Ayacucho.

THE AI, AND ITS LIMITS

- Retrieval plus verified rules never generate a number.

- A small open-weight planner: a LoRA adapter on SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct, trained locally on an NVIDIA RTX 4070 SUPER. On 50 hand-written questions the rules score 50/50 and the LoRA 40/50; both numbers are published, including where the model loses.

- In the live demo an optional hosted language model (OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini) can propose the plan and word the explanation. Every plan is checked by the rules and a guard rejects any figure or citation that is not in the NASA result. If the provider fails, the app answers with the rules and the panel says which engine answered.

- Honest verdicts: it reports "no trend detectable so far" (Antarctic sea ice) and "suggestive" (Piura rainfall) instead of overclaiming.

WHO BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Students and teachers who want real data with no account and no installation, in Spanish or English, on a laptop or a phone. It brings 45 years of NASA Earth observation into secondary and university classrooms and teaches the habit of quantifying uncertainty. Open source (MIT).

TOOLS

Python, FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy, pymannkendall, Leaflet, Chart.js, NASA GIBS and OpenStreetMap tiles; PyTorch, Transformers and PEFT for the LoRA; Railway and GitHub Pages for hosting.

WHAT IS CREATIVE

The detective framing; an assistant that must show its sources and refuses to invent numbers; honesty as a measurable feature (the guard, the display of disagreeing tests, published AI failures); and a conversational layer that answers a plain "hola" and then guides the student to the right variable.

KNOWN LIMITS

The optional language model is slower than the rules (2 to 7 s) and its guard checks that a number exists in the data, not which estimator it picks. Planned mission products (MODIS, OMI, AIRS, GPM, GLDAS) are declared but not yet analysable. The LoRA is not served publicly.

LINKS

Live app: https://huiracochaia.soulgeit.com

Backup site: https://soulgeit.github.io/nasa-earth-detective-o-nasa-reto-./

Code: https://github.com/soulgeit/nasa-earth-detective-o-nasa-reto-.

USE OF SI (full log: docs/AI_USE_LOG.md)

- Code: most of the code was written by SI coding agents under the team's direction: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.2) and Antigravity (Gemini 3.8 Flash). Every generated file starts with an "SI-assisted: <agent> (<model>)" header.Additionally, Hermes Agent, utilizing the local AI model Gemma 4 24B, proved helpful for extracting information.

- Data: the retrieval corpus was assembled with SI assistance (downloads, extraction, summaries); each document stores its URL, licence and sha256, and our own summaries are never shown as quotations. The 4,323 question-plan pairs used to train the LoRA were generated by script from templates.

- Models inside the product: SmolLM2-1.7B with a LoRA adapter, and in the live demo OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini.

- Audio: the narration of the pitch video is an AI-generated voice (ElevenLabs); the video says so on screen.

- Images: the project logo was generated with SI by the Antigravity agent. All screenshots are real captures of the running app.

- The idea, the choice of cases and the decision to publish every AI failure are the team's.
